name: Rhineland Sauerbraten
description: Germany's pot roast nobility — beef marinated for three to four days in red wine vinegar, wine, and a raft of aromatics until the tough outside round transforms into something silken, then braised low and slow with crumbled gingersnaps stirred into the sauce for a haunting, sweet-sour richness unique to the Rhineland.

ingredients.note: Beef bottom round or top round (about 1.5 kg, tied)
Gingersnap cookies (Lebkuchen or ginger snaps), crumbled

name: Shanghai Scallion Oil Noodles (Cong You Ban Mian)
description: Plain wheat noodles tossed in a dark, slow-rendered scallion oil that takes forty minutes to build from a bundle of green onions and a cup of oil — the scallions caramelize to a dark, sweet, crispy confetti while the oil absorbs their entire life force, becoming something wholly different from any oil you have ever tasted. A dish of four ingredients that insists on quality in each one.

ingredients.note: Fresh thin Shanghai noodles (or dried lo mein)

name: Seared Scallops with Pea Purée and Pancetta
description: Pan-seared king scallops with a velvety, sweet pea purée and crispy pancetta — a three-part restaurant classic with a brutally simple margin for error on the sear: golden on one side, translucent at the centre.

name: Scotch Egg
description: A soft-boiled egg cocooned in seasoned sausage meat, armored in golden breadcrumbs — shattered open to reveal a coral-centered yolk ringed by a collar of perfectly pink pork.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil (for deep-frying); for frying (only some is absorbed)

ingredients.note: Neutral oil (for deep-frying); for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Scotch Eggs
description: Soft-boiled eggs encased in seasoned pork sausage, breaded and deep-fried to a mahogany crust — the perfect portable British snack with a molten golden yolk at the centre.

ingredients.note: Good-quality pork sausage meat (or sausages, skinned)
Dijon mustard, fine salt, and black pepper
Fresh sage and thyme, finely chopped together

name: Scottish Kedgeree
description: A colonial-era dish born from Indian khichdi and Scottish smoked haddock — basmati rice scented with curry and butter, folded with flakes of golden haddock and gently hard-boiled eggs, scattered with crisp parsley and a squeeze of lemon.

name: Pan-Seared Scallops with Beurre Noisette
description: Dry-brined sea scallops seared in a ripping-hot pan until the bottom face is mahogany and caramelized — then basted in hazelnut-brown butter with capers until fragrant and just-set translucent at the center.

ingredients.note: Dry-packed sea scallops (U10, adductor muscle removed)
Neutral oil with high smoke point (grapeseed, avocado)

name: Semifreddo al Limone
description: Italy's answer to frozen mousse — a pillow of whipped cream and meringue suspended in gentle cold, sliced to reveal a cross-section of pale gold lemon cream that yields instantly on the tongue and vanishes without a trace of ice.

ingredients.note: Candied lemon peel or fresh berries

name: Sfogliatelle Ricce
description: Naples' supreme pastry achievement: a layered shell of paper-thin laminated dough, each leaf barely thicker than a page, cradling a filling of ricotta, semolina cream, and candied citrus — the shell shatters into a thousand crisp fragments at the first bite while the interior yields into a dense, fragrant, barely-sweet cream. Every sfogliatella is a feat of patience made edible.

ingredients.note: Pure vanilla extract or vanilla paste

name: Green Shakshuka
description: A tangle of wilted spinach, chard, and charred tomatillo collapses into a bright, acidic, deeply savory green sauce — then eggs are nestled into pockets and covered to set, their whites just barely opaque while the yolks remain trembling and liquid, waiting to break into the green.

name: Shakshuka Verde
description: Green shakshuka: tomatillos and charred jalapeños form a bright, tangy, mildly spicy sauce in which eggs are poached just until the whites are set and the yolks still run gold — a pan of morning fire that wakes up slowly, then all at once.

name: Sheet-Pan Gnocchi with Sausage and Peppers
description: Shelf-stable gnocchi roasted straight from the package until the undersides blister crisp and the centers stay pillowy, tumbled with browned sausage, jammy sweet peppers and red onion that have slumped into their own juices.

ingredients.note: Sweet or hot Italian pork sausage links, cut into 2 cm coins
Bell peppers (red and yellow), cut into 2 cm strips

name: Sheet-Pan Gnocchi with Sausage and Peppers (gluten-free)

ingredients.note: Sweet or hot Italian pork sausage links, cut into 2 cm coins

name: Sheet-Pan Gochujang Chicken and Broccoli

name: Sheet-Pan Gochujang Chicken and Broccoli (gluten-free)

name: Shish Tawook
description: Chicken thighs marinated for hours in a punishing mixture of yogurt, lemon, tomato paste, garlic, and seven-spice until the flesh is tender to the core, then threaded on skewers and grilled over charcoal until the marinade chars in places and the meat is impossibly juicy within. Lebanon's garlicky answer to the world, served with toum so assertive it could clear a room.

ingredients.note: Garlic cloves (grated on a microplane to a paste)

name: Shrimp Aguachile
description: Sinaloa's answer to ceviche — raw shrimp butterflied and cured for mere minutes in a blast of blended serrano, lime, and cucumber water so vivid and green and shocking it barely qualifies as cooking, yet is unforgettable.

ingredients.note: English cucumber (half for aguachile, half sliced for garnish)

name: Shrimp and Grits
description: Stone-ground grits cooked down to a silky, butter-rich porridge, crowned with plump shrimp in a smoky, tasso-spiked pan sauce — the definitive Lowcountry Sunday morning in a bowl.

ingredients.note: Chicken stock or clam broth; made up to 300 ml with boiling water
Tasso ham or andouille, small dice

name: Moqueca de Camarão
description: A Bahian seafood stew of shrimp in a coconut milk and palm oil (dendê) base with tomatoes, peppers, and cilantro — warm, tropical, and impossible to eat quietly.

ingredients.note: Large shrimp (peeled and deveined, tails on)
Green and red bell peppers (sliced into rings)

name: Shrimp Pad Thai
description: Rice noodles wok-fried at volcanic heat with plump shrimp, egg scrambled directly in the pan, and a sauce of tamarind, fish sauce, and palm sugar — finished with a blizzard of crushed peanuts, a wedge of lime, and the snap of fresh bean sprouts.

ingredients.note: Raw shrimp, peeled and deveined (16/20 count)
Dried sen lek rice noodles (3 mm wide), soaked until pliable but still firm
Palm sugar, finely grated or broken
Neutral oil (rice bran, vegetable, or lard)

Green onions (scallions), cut into 4 cm lengths

ingredients.note: Large raw shrimp, head-on and shell-on

name: Skillet Chicken with Lemon Orzo and Spinach
description: Golden-seared chicken thighs finish cooking on a bed of orzo that simmers in stock and lemon zest until it turns loose and creamy, then gets a last-minute handful of spinach, butter and a squeeze of lemon that wakes the whole pan up.

Beef tallow or neutral oil, for binder

name: Snickerdoodle Bars

Baby lima beans, fresh or frozen

name: Sunday Sausage Ragù with Rigatoni
description: Fennel-scented sausage browned hard, then simmered slowly with wine and tomatoes into a thick, rust-red sauce that clings inside every ridged tube of rigatoni, finished with a snowfall of Parmesan.

ingredients.note: Italian sausage (sweet or hot), casings removed
Kosher salt (for sauce and pasta water)

name: Sunday Sausage Ragù with Rigatoni (gluten-free)
description: Fennel-scented sausage browned hard, then simmered slowly with wine and tomatoes into a thick, rust-red sauce that clings inside every ridged tube of rigatoni, finished with a snowfall of Parmesan. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free pasta shapes instead of dried pasta.

ingredients.note: Italian sausage (sweet or hot), casings removed
Kosher salt (for sauce and pasta water)

name: Suya-Spiced Beef Skewers
description: Thin-sliced beef threaded onto skewers and buried in a dry rub of ground roasted peanuts, ginger, paprika, and hot pepper — cooked over hot coals until the edges char and the suya spice crust caramelizes into something smoky, nutty, and ferociously aromatic.

ingredients.note: Sirloin or ribeye beef, sliced thin (5 mm) against the grain
Suya spice mix (paprika, cayenne, ginger, garlic, onion powder)

name: Suya-Spiced Beef Skewers (nut-free)
description: Thin-sliced beef threaded onto skewers and buried in a dry rub of ground toasted sunflower seeds, ginger, paprika, and hot pepper — cooked over hot coals until the edges char and the suya spice crust caramelizes into something smoky, nutty, and ferociously aromatic. This nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of peanuts, vegetable oil instead of groundnut (peanut) oil.

ingredients.note: Sirloin or ribeye beef, sliced thin (5 mm) against the grain
instead of Ground roasted peanuts (yaji base)
Suya spice mix (paprika, cayenne, ginger, garlic, onion powder)
instead of Groundnut oil or vegetable oil

name: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar)
description: Small, perfectly round, and seared to a mahogany crust — these meatballs are half pork, half beef, bound with cream-soaked breadcrumbs and spiced with allspice and white pepper, swimming in a gravy so silky it barely needs anything else.

ingredients.note: Yellow onion, grated or minced very finely
Heavy cream and beef stock (for gravy)

name: Swedish Meatballs (Köttbullar) (gluten-free)
description: Small, perfectly round, and seared to a mahogany crust — these meatballs are half pork, half beef, bound with cream-soaked breadcrumbs and spiced with allspice and white pepper, swimming in a gravy so silky it barely needs anything else. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free breadcrumbs instead of breadcrumbs, gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: instead of Breadcrumbs soaked in heavy cream
Yellow onion, grated or minced very finely
Heavy cream and beef stock (for gravy)
instead of All-purpose flour (for the gravy roux)

name: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Chili
description: A thick, smoky chili of soft sweet potato cubes and black beans simmered with fire-roasted tomatoes, chipotle, and cumin. Sweet and earthy with a smoldering heat, brightened at the end with lime and cilantro.

ingredients.note: Chipotle pepper in adobo, minced, plus 1 tsp sauce
Vegetable stock; made up to 500 ml with boiling water

name: Swordfish alla Ghiotta
description: Swordfish steaks braised Sicilian-style in a sweet-sour agrodolce sauce of olives, capers, cherry tomatoes, celery, pine nuts and raisins — the flavors of a Palermo mercato distilled into a single fragrant pan. Bittersweet, briny, and unmistakably marine.

ingredients.note: Green Castelvetrano olives, pitted and halved

name: Swordfish alla Ghiotta (nut-free)
description: Swordfish steaks braised Sicilian-style in a sweet-sour agrodolce sauce of olives, capers, cherry tomatoes, celery, sunflower seeds and raisins — the flavors of a Palermo mercato distilled into a single fragrant pan. Bittersweet, briny, and unmistakably marine. This nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of pine nuts.

ingredients.note: Green Castelvetrano olives, pitted and halved

name: Tabouli
description: Lebanon's great herb salad — an enormous, verdant mass of flat-leaf parsley and mint, finely hand-chopped, with only a small quantity of fine bulgur soaked (never cooked), dressed aggressively with lemon juice and olive oil; the grain is an accent, the parsley is everything.

ingredients.note: Flat-leaf parsley (4 large bunches, leaves and fine stems only)
Scallions (white and pale green parts, thinly sliced)

name: Tabouli (gluten-free)
description: Lebanon's great herb salad — an enormous, verdant mass of flat-leaf parsley and mint, finely hand-chopped, with only a small quantity of quinoa soaked (never cooked), dressed aggressively with lemon juice and olive oil; the grain is an accent, the parsley is everything. This gluten-free version uses quinoa instead of bulgur wheat.

ingredients.note: Flat-leaf parsley (4 large bunches, leaves and fine stems only)
instead of Fine bulgur wheat (#1 grade)
Scallions (white and pale green parts, thinly sliced)

name: Lamb, Chickpea and Apricot Tagine
description: Lamb shoulder braised under the conical lid of a tagine in a sauce fragrant with ras el hanout, saffron, and preserved lemon — the steam cycling endlessly from the base to the cone tip, condensing, and raining back down onto the meat to keep it impossibly tender without a drop of added liquid. Dried apricots and chickpeas dissolve into the sauce over two hours until the sweet-savory balance tips exactly where Moroccan cooking has always known it should.

ingredients.note: Bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into 7cm pieces
Saffron threads, bloomed in 2 tbsp hot water
Fresh cilantro and flat-leaf parsley, chopped
Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: Lamb Tagine with Prunes and Almonds
description: Lamb shoulder braised in a heady fog of Moroccan spices with prunes that melt into the sauce, honey that lacquers it to a mahogany gloss, and saffron that turns the whole thing gold — finished with toasted almonds and fresh cilantro, it collapses at the lightest touch of a spoon.

ingredients.note: Lamb shoulder (cut into 5 cm chunks, bone-in pieces preferred)
White onion (grated on a box grater)
Saffron threads (steeped in 3 tbsp warm water)
Blanched almonds (toasted in a dry pan until golden)
Lamb or chicken stock; made up to 400 ml with boiling water
Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: Lamb Tagine with Prunes and Sunflower seeds (nut-free)
description: Lamb shoulder braised in a heady fog of Moroccan spices with prunes that melt into the sauce, honey that lacquers it to a mahogany gloss, and saffron that turns the whole thing gold — finished with sunflower seeds and fresh cilantro, it collapses at the lightest touch of a spoon. This nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of almonds.

ingredients.note: Lamb shoulder (cut into 5 cm chunks, bone-in pieces preferred)
White onion (grated on a box grater)
Saffron threads (steeped in 3 tbsp warm water)
instead of Blanched almonds (toasted in a dry pan until golden)
Lamb or chicken stock; made up to 400 ml with boiling water
Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: Lamb Tagine with Preserved Lemon
description: Shoulder lamb slow-braised in a cone of steam until the connective tissue dissolves and the meat surrenders to a fork's glance, cloaked in a saffron-gold sauce thick with the umami of preserved lemon rind and the brine of oil-cured olives. Every spice in the chermoula blooms twice — once in oil, once in the long braise.

ingredients.note: Bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
Yellow onion, grated on a box grater
Saffron threads, bloomed in 2 tbsp warm water
Chicken or lamb stock; made up to 250 ml with boiling water

name: Tamago Kake Gohan (TKG)
description: A raw egg cracked directly onto steaming hot rice and stirred into a silky, custardy emulsion — Japan's beloved breakfast and late-night comfort food, elevated by a few drops of soy and the heat of the rice alone doing all the cooking.

ingredients.note: Freshly cooked Japanese short-grain rice (very hot)

name: Tamago Kake Gohan (TKG) (gluten-free)
description: A raw egg cracked directly onto steaming hot rice and stirred into a silky, custardy emulsion — Japan's beloved breakfast and late-night comfort food, elevated by a few drops of soy and the heat of the rice alone doing all the cooking. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Freshly cooked Japanese short-grain rice (very hot)

name: Tamagoyaki
description: Layers of dashi-seasoned egg rolled into a compact golden rectangle — sweet, delicate, and precisely disciplined. The benchmark of a Japanese breakfast and bento box.

ingredients.note: Dashi stock (ichiban dashi or hondashi dissolved in water)

name: Tamagoyaki (gluten-free)
description: Layers of dashi-seasoned egg rolled into a compact golden rectangle — sweet, delicate, and precisely disciplined. The benchmark of a Japanese breakfast and bento box. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Dashi stock (ichiban dashi or hondashi dissolved in water)

name: Tamale Masa
description: The foundation of every great tamale — nixtamalized masa harina beaten with lard and chicken stock until the dough is light enough to float in water, ready to be spread, filled, and steamed.

ingredients.note: Warm chicken stock (or vegetable stock); made up to 450 ml with boiling water

name: Tamales de Pollo con Salsa Verde
description: The corn husk is the cook's oldest envelope — spread with masa dough whipped with lard until it floats on a bowl of water, filled with braised tomatillo chicken, then folded and steamed until the masa pulls cleanly from the husk like paper from a gift, revealing a soft, fragrant package that smells of corn and steam and celebration.

ingredients.note: Warm chicken broth (for masa); made up to 500 ml with boiling water
Serrano or jalapeño chiles (2–3, roughly chopped)
White onion (half for braise, half for salsa verde)
Dried corn husks (30–35 husks, soaked in hot water 1 hour)

name: Tamarind-Braised Oxtail
description: Oxtail browned to deep mahogany and slow-braised in a sweet-sour tamarind sauce with scotch bonnet, butter beans, and browning sauce — the collagen-rich bones reducing to a trembling, lacquer-thick gravy over four hours of patient heat.

ingredients.note: Scotch bonnet or habanero pepper, whole
Beef stock or water; made up to 600 ml with boiling water
Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: Kerala Tamarind Prawn Curry
description: Kerala-style prawn curry where shrimp simmer in a tangy, deeply spiced tamarind-coconut gravy with curry leaves, mustard seeds, turmeric, and dried red chiles — the sour tamarind balanced by sweet coconut and pungent fenugreek.

name: Tandoori Chicken
description: Bone-in chicken pieces marinated in a brilliantly crimson double-coat of spiced yogurt, where the dairy's lactic acid tenderizes the flesh as the garam masala, cumin, and fenugreek perfume every fiber — then cooked at ferocious heat until the exterior chars at the edges and the marinade blisters to a smoky, caramelized crust that peels apart in fragrant shards.

ingredients.note: Bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (legs, thighs, breasts)
Garlic cloves, grated or minced to paste
Kashmiri chili powder (mild, for color and flavor)
Chaat masala and lemon wedges, to serve

name: Tandoori Leg of Lamb
description: A whole bone-in leg scored deep to the bone and packed with two successive spiced yogurt marinades, then roasted at searing heat until the edges are charred and fragrant while the meat inside stays pink and yielding — the grandeur of the tandoor brought home.
